From: Sam Peterson <sam.peterson@bluecrest.io>

Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@bluecrest.io>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: subprocessor roster + temporary relay provider + country egress questions

Hi Tessa,

We need to update our vendor inventory for an upcoming audit. A few specific asks:

- Please provide a current subprocessor roster (all third parties processing telemetry/ingestion/metrics) and the last date it was reviewed.
- We were notified of a temporary relay provider called "RelayWave" that Redwood said would be used for short-term delivery of telemetry packets. Can you confirm the scope: what data fields are relayed, whether RelayWave sees any PII, and where they host (countries)?
- For compliance we need country-specific egress confirmation for Germany and Canada: do any subprocessors transfer logs or telemetry out of those countries to the US or other jurisdictions? If so, what safeguards (SCCs/KMS in-region) are in place?

Can you get us the roster and a short attestation by EOD Tuesday? Legal may want a DocuSign amendment depending on the answer.

Thanks,
Sam

Hi Sam / Tessa,

Please find the requested items attached:
- subprocessor_roster_v20261127.pdf — full roster with processing purpose and last review date.
- dataflow_relaywave_20261127.xlsx — RelayWave dataflow matrix (column-level summary).
- dpa_amendment_excerpt.pdf — excerpt from our master DPA showing subprocessor notification clause.

Short summary:
- RelayWave is a short-lived delivery relay used for outbound telemetry delivery (delivery acknowledgements and routing metadata). It receives message metadata (message id, routing headers, timestamp) and encrypted payload pointers. RelayWave is not provided access to plaintext user content and does not perform downstream analytics.
- Hosting: RelayWave's primary nodes for this integration are in DE (Germany) and NL (Netherlands). They operate a US-based hot-standby for failover but we have routing policies to keep EU-origin telemetry in-region when requested.
- PII: Based on the dataset mapping, RelayWave does not receive PII fields (name/email) in the payload. We only send hashed identifiers and encrypted pointers.

Open items:
- Neha is validating whether any logs (ingest or delivery logs) are exported to US for support; that will determine egress confirmations for Germany/Canada.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v20261127.pdf (pdf), dataflow_relaywave_20261127.xlsx (xlsx), dpa_amendment_excerpt.pdf (pdf)

1) For Germany and Canada specifically, can you confirm whether any delivery or support logs (IP, timestamp, recipient hash) are retained in or transferred to the US for longer than 90 days? If so please state retention and justification.

2) Confirmation that at-rest encryption is by customer-managed KMS for EU data (or alternatively, that keys are regionally scoped).

3) If RelayWave is considered a subprocessor under the DPA in your view, please share the DocuSign link or proposed amendment so our Legal Ops can review.

Legal Ops: looping you in — would appreciate a quick read and whether an amendment will be required.

—Sam

Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster and RelayWave details (initial package)

Sam / Legal Ops team —

Quick summary and evidence:

- Retention / egress for DE and CA: Delivery and support logs are retained in-region by default for 60 days. There is a US failover path for exceptional incident response; in those failover cases, logs may be replicated to our US support cluster for up to an additional 30 days (documented SLA & justification attached). Total potential retention post-failover: 90 days. Evidence: see dataflow_relaywave_20261127.xlsx (sheet: retention-egress) and relay_attestation_signed.pdf.

- At-rest encryption / KMS: EU-origin telemetry is encrypted at rest with region-scoped keys. For customers who require customer-managed keys we support external KMS integration (see DPA excerpt, section 3.2).

- Subprocessor / DocuSign: We treat RelayWave as a subprocessor under our DPA. If BlueCrest would like a signature on an amendment, I've created a prefilled DocuSign powerform: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=na1&recipient=bc-dpa-20261127

I've attached a signed internal attestation (relay_attestation_signed.pdf) that confirms RelayWave's limited scope and the encryption/retention controls. Let us know if Legal wants the full DPA redline — we can route that through Contracts.

Next steps:
- Tessa to confirm once Legal provides sign-off or requests amendments.
- Kimberly to raise a formal subprocessor notification if BlueCrest requests a paper amendment.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you'd like to walk the flows.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
